claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you some questions about your child or children.

**First, let's talk about the child's age:**

How old is your child? The eligibility rules differ depending on whether they are:
- Under 16 years old
- 16 to 19 years old  
- 20 or over

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children you'd like to check eligibility for, please let me know about each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to ask about Alex's education or training status:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education like A-levels, Scottish Highers, or approved vocational training)?
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school recently, but he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished his GCSEs and decided not to continue with sixth form or college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex finished his GCSEs and recently left school, and he's not currently in any education or training.

Since he left education recently, there may be an extension period where you could still be eligible for Child Benefit. Let me check the extension eligibility rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - there's a possibility you may still be eligible for a limited extension period!

**For 16-17 year olds who have recently left education, there's a 20-week extension available if certain conditions are met:**

To qualify for this extension, Alex would need to have:
1. Left approved education or training within the last 20 weeks, **AND**
2. Registered with a qualifying service such as:
   - A government careers service
   - Connexions (career development service)
   - The armed services

**Important questions:**
- **When exactly did Alex finish school?** (I need to know if it's been less than 20 weeks)
- **Has Alex registered with any careers service, Connexions, or the armed services?**

Please note: The extension ends either at the 20-week mark or when the child turns 18, whichever comes sooner.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished school about two months ago, so that's within the 20 weeks. But no, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. He's just been taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex finished school about two months ago (which is within the 20-week period), but he hasn't registered with any careers service, Connexions, or the armed services.

Unfortunately, this means the extension period doesn't apply to your situation. Both conditions need to be met - leaving education within 20 weeks AND registering with a qualifying service.

Let me navigate to the outcome based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: Not Eligible

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

### Why this decision was made:

Since Alex is 17 years old and has left education, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he meets specific conditions:

- **For 16-19 year olds in education/training:** They must be in approved full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels) or approved vocational training
- **For those who recently left education:** There's a 20-week extension period, BUT it only applies if the young person registers with a government careers service, Connexions service, or the armed services

While Alex left school within the 20-week window (about 2 months ago), he hasn't registered with any of the qualifying services, so the extension doesn't apply.

### What you can do:

**If Alex registers with a careers service or Connexions now**, you may become eligible for the remainder of the 20-week extension period (which would last approximately 3 more months from when he left school). 

**If Alex decides to return to education or start approved training**, you could become eligible again, as long as it's full-time non-advanced education or approved vocational training.

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, please feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility.

Under UK Child Benefit rules, the 20-week extension for 16-17 year olds who leave education is only available if they register with one of these qualifying services. Since Alex has not registered with any such service, the extension does not apply, and therefore he does not qualify as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.
